children.name: Pedionomus
children.description: A monotypic genus representing one of Australia's most evolutionarily distinctive bird lineages. The Plains-wanderer was long considered a buttonquail (Turnicidae) but DNA studies reveal it to be the sole surviving member of an ancient lineage that diverged before the radiation of modern shorebirds. It exhibits reversed sexual dimorphism and a polyandrous breeding system.

children.name: Pedionomus torquatus
children.description: The plains-wanderer (Pedionomus torquatus) is an atypical species of wading bird, the only representative of family Pedionomidae and genus Pedionomus. It is endemic to Australia. Its historic range included much of eastern Australia, including Victoria, New South Wales, South Australia and the Northern Territory, but in recent years, it has become endangered with remaining known populations concentrated in the Riverina region of New South Wales and western Queensland.
